svg.title: Contiguous KV pre-allocation versus PagedAttention
svg.desc: Two panels. On the left, contiguous pre-allocation: four sequences each get a contiguous slab sized for the 2048-token maximum length. Only a small prefix of each slab holds real tokens; the rest is hatched in rust as reserved but never written, at 91, 70, 98 and 44 percent respectively, about 76 percent of the region overall. A free gap between slabs is too small to hold another 2048-token slab and is therefore unusable: external fragmentation. On the right, PagedAttention: a uniform pool of fixed-size 16-token blocks, with blocks coloured by owning sequence and scattered non-contiguously through the pool, free blocks left empty, and per-sequence block tables mapping logical block index to physical block number beside it. An arrow runs from one block-table row to the physical block it names. Internal fragmentation is bounded by one partly filled block per sequence.

text.font-family: Iowan Old Style, Palatino, Georgia, serif

svg.text: Two ways to hold a KV cache — and why one of them is segmentation
